stories.title: AI Has Ideas About Intellectual Disabilities. It’s Not Always Accurate
stories.simple_summary: Artificial intelligence systems sometimes give wrong or biased information when answering questions about intellectual disabilities. These mistakes can spread bad ideas to people who trust the AI.
stories.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know has an intellectual disability, be careful trusting AI chatbots for medical or personal advice — they can get things wrong just like people can.

stories.title: China warns of retaliation if US sticks with robot ban
stories.simple_summary: China said it will punish the United States if America continues restricting the sale of certain advanced robots to China. This is a trade disagreement between two countries.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to large companies and government — nothing a small business owner needs to worry about unless you export advanced equipment.

stories.title: Opinion | OpenAI agent’s autonomous hack should scare world into regulating AI
stories.simple_summary: Someone wrote that an AI agent successfully hacked into a computer system on its own, and argues this shows the world needs stronger rules for AI right now. This is someone's opinion piece, not confirmed news.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly for investors and tech people to debate — it doesn't affect your daily life today, though it reflects ongoing concerns about AI safety.

stories.title: EU Will Reportedly Label ChatGPT and Roblox ‘Very Large Online Platforms’ (Derogatory)
stories.simple_summary: The European Union plans to officially label ChatGPT and Roblox as "very large online platforms" and will likely regulate them more closely. This is a government classification.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT in Europe, rules about how these services work may change, but for most small-business owners, this won't change much in the near term.

stories.title: Microsoft is openly competing with OpenAI, Anthropic more than ever
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is creating its own AI systems and tools to compete directly against OpenAI and Anthropic. They told investors they plan to keep growing this business.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — it means more AI companies are competing, which is good for innovation, but you won't notice much difference in your daily life.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg predicts that billions of people will have personal AI agents in five years
stories.simple_summary: Mark Zuckerberg says within five years, billions of people will have personal AI assistants that work for them. He's trying to convince investors that Meta's big spending on AI will pay off.
stories.why_it_matters: Zuckerberg is making a prediction about the future to convince investors — whether this happens depends on many factors, so don't plan your business around this yet.

stories.title: Microsoft logs $3.2B from Anthropic investment, but OpenAI was a mixed bag
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft made $3.2 billion from its investment in Anthropic (an AI company), though its other AI investments had mixed results. This is financial reporting for investors.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investor news — it shows Microsoft is betting on AI companies, but doesn't affect your small business operations.

stories.title: Zuckerberg says Meta’s enterprise AI opportunity extends beyond agents
stories.simple_summary: Mark Zuckerberg says Meta sees business opportunities in selling AI agents and tools to other companies, not just using AI for its own products. The company wants to make money from AI in different ways.
stories.why_it_matters: Meta may eventually offer AI services that some businesses could purchase, but for now this is mostly planning — nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Microsoft confirms Copilot ‘super app’ coming this year
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is building a new AI app that combines chat, coding help, and automation features all in one place. It will come out sometime this year and work on both phones and business computers.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Microsoft tools for your small business, you may get a new AI assistant app to try — it could save time on routine tasks, but wait to see what it actually does before deciding if it helps you.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg is planning a big push into personal AI agents
stories.simple_summary: Meta plans to create personal AI agents that can do tasks for you automatically, like a helper that works on your computer or phone. This is part of their big plan to focus on AI.
stories.why_it_matters: In the future, you might have an AI helper that schedules appointments or handles simple tasks for you, but this is still being developed and it's too early to know if it will be useful.

stories.title: Elon Musk's xAI sues Minnesota over its first-in-the-nation law banning 'nudification' technology
stories.simple_summary: Elon Musk's AI company xAI is suing Minnesota over a new law that bans technology that creates fake nude photos of people. xAI disagrees with the law.
stories.why_it_matters: Minnesota passed a law to protect people from a harmful technology — this is a legal dispute between a company and a state, and doesn't affect most people unless you live in Minnesota or use that specific technology.

stories.title: Discover what’s next for AI, from the SaaS reckoning to the agent security gap, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is promoting a technology conference happening in 2026 where people will discuss the latest AI developments. This is an advertisement for an event.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a conference advertisement — unless you're interested in attending a tech conference or work in the tech industry, you can skip this.
